rules.label: Two voices before a number
rules.text: Every forecast carries a Becoming case and a Returning case before it carries a probability.

rules.label: Score with a proper rule
rules.text: Every resolved forecast is scored by the Brier score, against a permanent 50% as the baseline.

rules.label: Keep score in public, no backfill
rules.text: Locked fields never change after merge; misses stay visible and a changed view is a new file.

rules.label: One owner per probability
rules.text: Only the named forecaster writes a probability; agents draft, and challengers read only the record.

rules.label: Breadth over boldness
rules.text: Many small, dated, scorable questions instead of a few grand calls.

rules.label: Start from risk
rules.text: Nothing is credited to skill until the factor part and the residual have been separated.

thinkers.name: Baruch Spinoza
thinkers.idea: The order and connection of ideas is the same as the order and connection of things; falsity is a lack of knowledge, not something positive.

thinkers.name: Philipp Mainländer
thinkers.idea: Every striving uses itself up: the world moves from being towards its own extinction.

thinkers.name: Glenn W. Brier
thinkers.work: Verification of forecasts expressed in terms of probability
thinkers.idea: A probability forecast can be scored by its squared distance from what happened, which rewards honest, calibrated numbers.

thinkers.name: Philip E. Tetlock
thinkers.work: Expert Political Judgment (2005); Superforecasting, with Dan Gardner (2015)
thinkers.idea: Judgement improves only where it is scored over many questions; forecasters who keep score, think in fine-grained probabilities and update beat those who don't.

thinkers.name: Daniel Kahneman
thinkers.work: Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011); Noise, with Olivier Sibony and Cass R. Sunstein (2021)
thinkers.idea: Judgements are noisy as well as biased; independent assessments, made before people see each other's views, reduce the noise.

thinkers.name: Harry Markowitz
thinkers.idea: Risk belongs to the portfolio, through how its parts move together, not to any single holding.

thinkers.name: Richard C. Grinold and Ronald N. Kahn
thinkers.idea: The fundamental law of active management: skill per call multiplied by the square root of the number of independent calls.

thinkers.name: Giuseppe A. Paleologo
thinkers.work: Advanced Portfolio Management: A Quant's Guide for Fundamental Investors
thinkers.idea: Separate every position into factor and idiosyncratic risk, and judge and size an idea by the part that is truly its own.
